gbm_population_evidence.quote: Histologically confirmed newly diagnosed grade IV glioma (gliosarcoma allowed)

candidate_evidence.quote: Chloroquine is normally used to treat strains of malaria and prior preclinical and clinical data suggests that it may increase the efficacy of both radiation and tumor treating fields therapy.

treatment_setting_evidence.quote: Treatment of Adults with Newly Diagnosed Glioblastoma with Partial Brain Radiation Therapy Plus Temozolomide and Chloroquine Followed by Tumor Treating Fields Plus Temozolomide and Chloroquine

role_evidence.quote: Chloroquine is normally used to treat strains of malaria and prior preclinical and clinical data suggests that it may increase the efficacy of both radiation and tumor treating fields therapy.

agents.stated_antitumour_mechanism: may increase the efficacy of both radiation and tumor treating fields therapy

role_evidence.quote: receive temozolomide orally (PO) and chloroquine PO daily from day 1 for the duration of radiation therapy up to day 49

agents.drug_class_hint: alkylating agent, GBM standard of care

role_evidence.quote: To measure treatment effect via advanced magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) and alpha-\[11C\]methyl-L-tryptophan (AMT)-positron emission tomography (PET).

agents.drug_class_hint: PET imaging tracer (carbon-11 labelled tryptophan analogue)

coder_notes: Chloroquine is the only investigational drug, added to standard RT + temozolomide followed by TTFields + temozolomide (single arm). AMT-PET tracer is not a registered intervention but is used for secondary outcome imaging -> diagnostic_agent; AMT-PET is imaging-only, not recorded as a molecular biomarker. G6PD deficiency exclusion is a germline safety marker (not recorded). Population: 'grade IV glioma' in inclusion with conditions Glioblastoma; Gliosarcoma -> gbm_only; no IDH or WHO edition reference -> cns5 unclear.
